newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs seesaw, end modestly up in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs seesaw, end modestly up in heavy trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks seesawed to end slightly higher in speculative trades amid rumors that the announcement of qualified Band B bidders could be delayed, brokers said.

The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 48 most traded shares closed up 0.39 percent at 11,345 points. Volume was higher than usual at 937.1 million reais ($875.5 million), taking some traders by surprise as they had expected slow trade after Thursday's Corpus Christi holiday.
Shares opened lower on profit-taking, weighed down by losses on Wall Street.
Prices then rebounded, driven by bellwether Telebras stock to lose ground before it closed at 147.70 reais.
Communications Ministry said the release of the names of the qualified bidders is still scheduled for Wednesday at 0900 local time/0800 EDT/1200 GMT.
Telebras stock had been rising on expectations that consortia competing for the Band B presented exceptionally high bids to run the cellular services.
Among other blue chips, only Petrobras posted gains, rising 2.4 percent to 256 reais at the close. Private 23.65 reais. Federal power utility Eletrobras dropped 0.38 percent to close at 527 reais.

Minas Gerais state's Cemig, which slipped Wednesday following the sale of a 32.9 percent voting stake, rebounded, rising 0.6 percent to 46.79 reais. The company's preferred rose 3.16 percent to 49 reais.
